_doc: Headwaters source registry - ATLAS-SCOPE sources. The Onboarding Atlas serves Tamil Nadu districts, blocks and Gram Panchayats (schemas/nvdm/scopes.json: tn-thanjavur, tn-tiruchirappalli are district scopes). Identity comes from TNRD (the 2021 LGD-coded PDF for stable codes, the current master for membership), JJM IMIS (service villages) and Census 2011 (settlement composition); TNGIS supplies polygons and water bodies under an UNVERIFIED licence. IN-GRES (chennai.json: ingres-gw-assessment-tn) and Open-Meteo (platform.json: open-meteo-archive) are NOT duplicated here - their dependsOn lists carry the atlas paths. As with every other registry file, cadence and tier are DOCUMENTATION ONLY and do not gate polling - see the note in basins.json. 2026-09-01: Satara (Maharashtra, mh-satara) joins as the first district outside Tamil Nadu. Its identity comes from the Local Government Directory as republished on data.gov.in (three resources below), its Census rows from the Maharashtra DCHB release, its polygons from DataMeet (ODbL, served); IN-GRES Maharashtra is pune.json's ingres-groundwater-maharashtra with atlas dependsOn added there.

sources.publisher: Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
sources.license: TN government publication, cited with attribution
sources.cadence: closed edition (PDF dated 2021-03-11; republished in place only if TNRD re-cuts it)
sources.refreshMethod: scripts/atlas-refresh-tn-district.ts --district <slug> --fetch --as-of <date> (pdftotext parse; fails closed when a district's Gram Panchayat count drifts from pipeline-inputs/atlas/<state>/<district>/refresh-plan.json)
sources.notes: The stable-code edition: every TNRD village panchayat with its LGD district, block and GP codes, 12,525 rows statewide. The PDF's own CreationDate is 2021-03-11 and the server's Last-Modified agrees (verified 2026-08-29), which is what http-meta watches: a re-cut PDF at the same URL is the only edition event. It is older than the current master (tnrd-panchayat-master) and the two are kept as separate receipts on purpose - current membership and stable codes are never conflated. as_of 2021-03-11 in every envelope that cites it.

sources.license: TN government publication, cited with attribution
sources.cadence: continuous membership updates; district option set changes only on reorganisation
sources.refreshMethod: scripts/atlas-refresh-tn-district.ts --district <slug> --fetch --as-of <date> (POST cmd=9 for blocks, cmd=3 per block for Gram Panchayats; fails closed on count drift)
sources.notes: The current village panchayat master behind the public property-tax dues form: district > block > Gram Panchayat, each with a local code. The page serves no ETag or Last-Modified (verified 2026-08-29), so http-meta cannot watch it; its own 'last updated' stamp is today's date on every visit (a daily database stamp, not an edition), so page-hash on the whole page would fire daily. What is watched instead is the district option set (select#dcode), which changes only when Tamil Nadu reorganises districts. Block and Gram Panchayat membership can only be seen through AJAX postbacks, so membership drift is caught by the monthly acquisition re-run, which compares counts against the reviewed plan and stops on any difference. The page's own last-updated date is recorded per acquisition as the source's as_of.

lastSeen.edition: district option set as served 2026-08-29 (38 districts)

sources.publisher: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti (JJM IMIS)
sources.license: Government of India publication, cited with attribution
sources.cadence: continuous (habitation, source and sample rows update as the programme reports)
sources.refreshMethod: scripts/atlas-refresh-tn-district.ts --fetch (village enumeration via ASP.NET postbacks ddState > ddDistrict) then scripts/atlas-jjm-tn-district.ts --district <slug> --fetch --as-of <date> (JSON page methods BindHabitationInfo, BindSourceInfo, BindSampleTestedInfo per village, serial and paced). Monthly scheduled re-run is the freshness question (follow-up: check-data-freshness.ts is city-keyed).
sources.notes: Village information page of the JJM citizen corner. The district option set is only rendered after an ASP.NET __doPostBack on ddState, and the checker fetches with GET, so no method here can see the district set directly (tried 2026-08-29: the initial page carries the 36 state options and an empty ddDistrict; ETag is a Cache-Control string, not a validator; the body carries a per-request ViewState so a whole-page hash is never stable). What IS watchable is the state option set (select#ddState): a change there means the form was rebuilt, which is the same event that would move the district set. District and village enumeration drift is caught by the acquisition itself, which fails closed when the count differs from the reviewed plan. The page methods take state, district and village ids only (no session, no ViewState); encodeTxt-style obfuscation, if introduced, breaks the parser loudly rather than publishing noise. Licence: GoI programme portal, cited with attribution; no explicit reuse terms beyond the standard GoI website policy.

sources.publisher: Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India
sources.license: Government of India publication, cited with attribution
sources.cadence: closed (Census 2011 release; village reference year 2009). The 2021 census did not take place, so no newer village-level enumeration exists.
sources.refreshMethod: scripts/atlas-refresh-tn-district.ts --fetch (downloads DH_2011_DCHB_Village_Release_3300.xlsx via system curl - the NADA certificate chain is incomplete for Node's bundled CAs; identity columns via scripts/atlas_extract_census_village_amenities.py) then scripts/atlas-census-tn-district.ts --district <slug> --workbook <xlsx> --as-of <date> (water and land-use columns via scripts/atlas_extract_census_village_attributes.py)
sources.notes: District Census Handbook village amenities, Tamil Nadu (state 33) village release, the one NADA catalog entry that carries the statewide XLSX (DH_2011_DCHB_Village_Release_3300.xlsx, 33.7 MB, sha256 ab604ec5...). Closed source: as_of 2011 in every envelope. The NADA page sends no validators (verified 2026-08-29), so page-hash on the resource-downloads block watches the only thing that could change - the file list and versions the catalog offers. Village rows may declare several CD-block and Gram Panchayat memberships; the atlas keeps every pair and never assigns a multi-Panchayat village silently. Reference year for the amenity and land-use tables is 2009: a historical baseline, never current service. TLS: censusindia.gov.in serves a certificate chain that macOS and curl accept but Node's bundled CA verifier does not (fetch fails with 'TypeError: fetch failed' while curl returns 200; the same reason the acquisition downloads the workbook through system curl), so insecureTLS is set the way the NMCG and CPCB entries set it - verification skipped for this host only.

lastSeen.edition: NADA catalog 45377 resource list as served 2026-08-29 (village release xlsx 49381)

sources.publisher: Department of Economics and Statistics, Government of Tamil Nadu
sources.license: TN government publication, cited with attribution
sources.cadence: yearly (a new edition appears as a new year row with a Drive 'View' link on the listing)
sources.refreshMethod: update pipeline-inputs/atlas/<state>/<district>/irrigation-des.json from the new edition's Table III-B (a person re-verifies every figure against the PDF), then npm run atlas:irrigation -- --district <slug> per district
playbook: A new edition appears on the DES listing as a new year row whose Download cell is a Google Drive 'View' link; the Drive file id is in that link's href.
Download the PDF via drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=<fileid>&export=download&confirm=t (the drive.google.com viewer URL does not serve the bytes directly); record its sha256.

pdftotext -layout on the PDF, then find 'AREA IRRIGATED BY DIFFERENT SOURCES': Table III-B runs seven printed pages (2024-25 edition: pages 125-131), one column group per page - canals, tanks, tube/bore wells, open wells, supplementary wells, other sources, then the totals page (gross, net, area irrigated more than once, intensity).

Read each district's NET total column per source plus its totals-page row. Supplementary wells ('by all other types of wells') water land already counted under another source: record them in the separate field, never as a sixth component of the net total.

Component sums can miss the printed net total by a hectare of the report's own rounding (Tiruchirapalli 2024-25: components 90284 vs printed 90283); the producer tolerates 2 ha and requires a note stating any discrepancy. More than 2 ha apart means a misread row - stop and re-verify.

Spelling drift: the report prints 'Tiruchirapalli'; find district rows by Sl. No. and name together, and cross-check the STATE row against the report's own state totals before trusting the extraction.
Update pipeline-inputs/atlas/tn/<district>/irrigation-des.json with the new figures, page cites, PDF sha256 and extractedOn, then npm run atlas:irrigation -- --district <slug> for both districts.
sources.notes: The annual Season and Crop Report of the TN Directorate of Economics and Statistics: the current district irrigation source mix (Table III-B, net area irrigated by canals, tanks, tube/bore wells, open wells and other sources), the reading that replaced Census 2011 at the head of the district pages. The listing page is a stable Drupal node (two fetches hash identically, verified 2026-09-01) whose edition table is watched with page-hash on table.table-bordered: a new edition is a new year row. The report itself lives behind a Google Drive link, so http-meta has nothing to watch; the 2024-25 edition is Drive file 1uONHRwuvU9-EhDGD1v0XC0OWqAVOZtV6, PDF sha256 49bbd356b1aab315a53e9a62ef0ba9a124a90c5975231146fb1bab0498f7eb75.

lastSeen.edition: Season and Crop Report 2024-25 (year rows 2014-2015 through 2024-2025)

sources.license: LICENCE UNVERIFIED - see notes. TNGIS/TNeGA terms restrict public display, redistribution and commercial use to prior approval; the reuse confirmation requested 2026-07-27 has no reply. Only derived counts, areas, centroids and digests are published; cited with attribution.
sources.cadence: continuous (five departments' registers merged; no survey date published)
sources.refreshMethod: scripts/atlas-water-bodies-tn-district.ts --district <slug> --as-of <date> --fetch (WFS GetFeature on generic_viewer:all_water_bodies filtered by rd_lgddcod; joins on panchayat_lgdvcode, stops if the join rate drops below half)
sources.notes: LICENCE UNVERIFIED - UNRESOLVED. https://tngis.tn.gov.in/user.html states: 'GIS based data available in TNGIS should be used for informational purpose only and Not for legal use/not to be shared / published in the public media in any form or in the social media without any prior approval / permission from TNGIS/TNeGA.' A reuse confirmation was requested on 2026-07-27 (the corridor's D4 blocker) and has had no reply. Until it does, the served water-bodies shards carry null geometry and no water-body names: only per-Panchayat counts, areas computed from the withheld polygons, contributing departments and a digest of the sorted names. The GetCapabilities document is 828 KB and every WFS response is served without ETag or Last-Modified, so content-hash on DescribeFeatureType for this layer is the watch: it is small (3.5 KB), stable, and changes exactly when the schema does - including the panchayat_lgdvcode join column the whole family depends on. A feature-count change is NOT an edition here (the register is continuously edited); re-acquisition cadence is a freshness question. Extraction gotcha: the statewide layer carries town and corporation rows with panchayat_lgdvcode 0; they are dropped, never pooled under a fake Panchayat.

sources.license: LICENCE UNVERIFIED - see notes. TNGIS/TNeGA terms restrict public display, redistribution and commercial use to prior approval; the reuse confirmation requested 2026-07-27 has no reply. Only derived counts, areas, centroids and digests are published; cited with attribution.
sources.cadence: episodic (boundaries change at reorganisation; no mapping year published)
sources.refreshMethod: scripts/atlas-refresh-tn-district.ts --district <slug> --fetch-boundary --as-of <date> (WFS GetFeature on tnrd:panchayat_boundary filtered by district_lgd_code = the TNRD district code) and scripts/atlas-project-groundwater.ts --fetch (admin_master:administrative_boundary_taluk filtered by the LGD district code)
sources.notes: LICENCE UNVERIFIED - same terms and same pending request as tngis-generic-viewer-water-bodies. Two layers ride on this entry because they share the endpoint, the terms and the consumers: tnrd:panchayat_boundary (village_lgd_code, block_lgd_code, district_lgd_code - the join is by LGD code, no name folding) and admin_master:administrative_boundary_taluk (sub_district_code, taluk_name). CODE-SPACE TRAP: the panchayat layer's district_lgd_code is the TNRD district code (Thanjavur 540) while the taluk layer's district_lgd_code is the LGD district code (Thanjavur 586); both come from the reviewed plan, never from the command line, after a neighbouring district's taluks were fetched once by hand. What is published: bbox-centre centroids, areas, vertex counts and geometry digests in directory.json; taluk containment as the groundwater projection; no polygon leaves the cache until approval is recorded. Watched with content-hash on DescribeFeatureType for the panchayat layer (1.6 KB, no validators served).

sources.publisher: Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Government of India, via the Open Government Data Platform (data.gov.in)
sources.cadence: monthly (the portal republishes the LGD on the 1st of each month)
sources.refreshMethod: scripts/atlas-refresh-lgd-district.ts --district <slug> --fetch --as-of <date> (bulk CSV export discovered from the portal's resource metadata; fails closed when the Panchayat or coverage count drifts from pipeline-inputs/atlas/<state>/<district>/refresh-plan.json)
sources.notes: The identity master for districts outside Tamil Nadu: every rural local body with the village(s) it covers, LGD codes throughout. lgdirectory.gov.in itself is captcha-gated on every view and download, so this republication is what a machine reads. Watched through the portal's own list API (updated_date of the resource), with the repository's public sample key (ten rows a call is enough to read one date). The export lists ONE covering village for most Panchayats rather than every member (Maharashtra: 29,460 coverage rows for 28,045 Panchayats against 43,705 village-to-Panchayat rows in the 2022 captcha download), so it settles the Panchayat list and a Panchayat's taluka, and only partially its settlement composition; the full mapping is the captcha download 'Village To Gram Panchayat Mapping', a reviewed input when a person supplies it. Licence: data.gov.in publishes under the Government Open Data License - India, attribution to the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Government of India, via the Open Government Data Platform (data.gov.in)
sources.cadence: monthly by declaration; the resource's own updated_date last moved 2022-11-17, its rows carry 2026 last_updated stamps
sources.refreshMethod: scripts/atlas-refresh-lgd-district.ts --district <slug> --fetch --as-of <date> (district filter on the bulk export)
sources.notes: Every LGD village with its Census 2011 code, sub-district and district: the join between the LGD register, the Census workbook and the DataMeet polygons. The export header labels the local-name column 'VillageCode' a second time, so the parser reads positions and checks the header as published. Satara 2026-09: 1,764 villages, 1,693 with an LGD code equal to the Census 2011 code, the rest newer villages. The sibling 'Villages with PIN Codes' resource (f17a1608) updates daily and agreed on 1,763 of them; it is not registered because it adds nothing the identity needs.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Government of India, via the Open Government Data Platform (data.gov.in)
sources.refreshMethod: scripts/atlas-refresh-lgd-district.ts --district <slug> --fetch --as-of <date> (district filter on the bulk export)
sources.notes: The taluka list. It is the block layer where a state's Panchayat Samitis are coterminous with its talukas (Satara: eleven of each, same names; the refresh plan records blockModel 'sub-district'), and the unit IN-GRES assesses in Maharashtra, so the groundwater projection there is a code join through this list rather than a polygon intersection. The LGD development-block resource is not on data.gov.in.

sources.publisher: Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India
sources.license: Government of India publication, cited with attribution
sources.cadence: closed edition (Census 2011; the 2021 census did not take place)
sources.refreshMethod: scripts/atlas-refresh-lgd-district.ts --district <slug> --fetch (downloads DH_2011_DCHB_Village_Release_2700.xlsx, 82 MB, once into the content-addressed cache and reuses it hash-verified) then scripts/atlas-census-tn-district.ts --district <slug> --workbook <cached xlsx> --as-of <date>
sources.notes: The Maharashtra village release (worksheet Village_Data_2700) of the same DCHB series Tamil Nadu uses (catalog 45377, release 3300). One trap and one gap: the Tamil Nadu catalog's download id will serve a file under a Maharashtra filename, so the Maharashtra workbook is pinned to catalog 828 download 36182 and its sha256 6697776f33d6a08f6eeaf77c1f7652bf56c32d51f87ea40277f39c2fae1eca67; and this release leaves the Gram Panchayat code and name columns blank for every village (1,745 of 1,745 in Satara), so settlement composition comes from the LGD coverage register and the Census rows join by village code alone. censusindia.gov.in serves an incomplete TLS chain (insecureTLS for the checker; the producer downloads with curl and the system trust store).

lastSeen.edition: baselined 2026-09-01 for Satara (catalog 828, Maharashtra village release 2700)

sources.cadence: closed edition in practice (a 2001 Census village map digitised by volunteers; the repository moved once, 2026-07, and was found again on GitHub 2026-09)
sources.refreshMethod: scripts/atlas-refresh-lgd-district.ts --district <slug> --fetch-boundary --as-of <date> (mh2.geojson 78 MB plus mh/mh.csv, content-addressed; the district's features are sliced by DISTRICT and joined to the 2011 codes through the CEN_2001 crosswalk) then scripts/atlas-boundaries-lgd-district.ts --district <slug> --as-of <date>
sources.notes: Village polygons keyed on the 2001 Census code (CEN_2001), with DataMeet's own mh.csv mapping them to the 2011 village code the LGD carries. A Panchayat's geometry is the MultiPolygon of its LGD-listed member villages, never dissolved, so the parts stay auditable; Satara 2026-09: 1,865 features, 1,665 of the 1,764 LGD villages drawn. Indicative, not survey grade: a 2001-era community digitisation, 2001-to-2011 splits and merges resolved by the crosswalk only. ODbL: attribution required and share-alike on the derived database, which is why the derived Panchayat polygons are served (boundaries/<block>.geojson) under the same licence, unlike the TNGIS layer. GitHub raw serves an ETag, so http-meta sees a re-cut file.
